trivia.statement: It was crafted during the Chenghua Emperor's reign.
The blue pigment was imported from Persia.
The gold finish is applied using mercury.
It runs on a standard AA battery.
It was manufactured in 18th Century France.
The canvas is made of woven linen.
The urn's engraved motifs are characteristic of Safavid-era metalwork from 17th century Isfahan.
Bronze vessels of this type were used in royal hammams for storing rosewater.
The patina was artificially applied in a 1920s London workshop to increase its apparent age.

objects.name: Ivan the Terrible and His Son

trivia.statement: Painted by Ilya Repin in 1885, it depicts the moment Tsar Ivan IV mortally wounds his own son.
The painting was slashed by a vandal in 1913 and again in 2018 at the Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow.
Repin based the composition on a photograph he secretly took inside the Kremlin archives.
The blue-green glaze is produced from crushed quartz and copper oxide, a technique dating to 3500 BCE.
The accompanying ushabti figurine was placed in tombs to serve the deceased in the afterlife.
This vessel was recovered from the tomb of Cleopatra VII during a 1902 British excavation.
